title: Helios private deploy - KV cache & tail-latency scratch notes
content:
Summary:
Helios (on-prem/private) reported repeated 5–10s tail latency spikes for text-generation routes 2025-02-11 22:00–02:00 UTC. Symptoms include transient 502/503s, large variance in per-token latency, and several worker restarts. This doc is my scratchpad: commands tried, raw error snippets, timeline, hypotheses, and draft comms to customer/infra teams.

Quick hypothesis (working):
- Recent model rollout (v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0) changed KV cache key shape and increased cache miss ratio, causing bigger KV re-materialization and slower token generation.
- That extra memory pressure caused GPU memory to fragment and sometimes trigger fallback or longer GC operations in our runtime, producing very high tail latencies and occasional request failures.
- Secondary: node-level I/O/blocking (NVMe contention) amplified during pruning/flush.

Commands & observations (raw) — run interactively:
- kubectl -n redwood logs pod/helios-runtime-0 -c runtime --since=2h | grep "kvcache"
  -> "kvcache: hit_rate=0.12 miss_rate=0.88 entries=3421" (22:14:03 UTC)
- /opt/redwood/bin/inferctl status --endpoint=helios:8080
  -> active-model: v2.4.0; kvcache-size: 64MB; batchers: 6/6; queue-depth spikes 200->1200
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
  -> processes: runtime PID 4132 gpu-memory 14348MiB, occasionally briefly 16000MiB then OOM log
- journalctl -u redwood-runtime | tail -n 200
  -> repeated: "runtime: cuda allocation failed: out of memory" followed by "runtime: falling back to CPU path"
- dmesg | grep -i oom
  -> no kernel OOM killer entries; but many "nv_mem_agent: reclaim requested" lines
- redis-cli -h 10.2.5.8 INFO | grep -E "keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses"
  -> hits: 4.5M, misses: 9.1M  (miss ratio ~0.67 during window)

Error snippets captured:
- "2025-02-12T22:11:14Z ERROR runtime - cuda: out of memory while allocating 512MB (requested by kvcache rehydrate)"
- "rpc: unexpected EOF while reading response body"
- "http: 502 upstream read timeout" (loadbalancer logs)
- "kvcache: prune loop took 2.4s (threshold 0.1s)"

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 2025-02-11 21:50: deployment of model v2.4.0 completed (Helios release pipeline)
- 2025-02-11 22:00: first customer alert: spike in 95th/99th latency (observed by Helios SRE)
- 2025-02-11 22:03: internal alert -> on-call paged (Ravi)
- 2025-02-11 22:10: started collecting runtime logs, nvml and redis metrics
- 2025-02-11 22:20: noticed kvcache miss spikes and several GPU allocation failures
- 2025-02-11 22:35: scaled runtime replicas +2 as short mitigation (reduced error volume, latency still high)
- 2025-02-11 23:15: rollback candidate prepared (v2.3.1) but held for analysis
- 2025-02-12 00:05: started targeted pprof on runtime to inspect heap growth during long tail requests

Actions so far (by time):
- Collected pprof heap + goroutine dumps from pid 4132 (saved in /tmp/helios-dumps/)
- Increased kvcache memory quota from 64MB -> 128MB as experiment (observed lower miss ratio but temporary improvement)
- Forced a rolling restart of one node that had repeated allocation failures (node-3); after bounce, error volume dropped ~30% for 20m
- Reproduced locally with smaller model + synthetic load; observed similar kvcache thrash when key prefix changed

Open questions / next investigative steps:
- Did v2.4.0 change tokenization or cache key construction? Need diff of model-serving config (ask model-onboarding).
- Is NVMe or PCIe transient causing allocations to block? Check slow I/O traces and iostat during spike windows.
- Could memory fragmentation in our allocator (cuda malloc patterns) cause repeated slow allocations? Try upgrading cuda-allocator layer in a canary.
- How bad is cross-pod KV cache churning? Are we invalidating prefixes aggressively?

Mitigations to propose:
- Short-term: pin Helios to v2.3.1 until a fix; increase kvcache quota and gentle autoscale to absorb burst.
- Medium-term: add better cache key compatibility layer + migration shim that warms keys on rollout.
- Long-term: introduce allocation guardrails and pre-reserve KV rehydrate buffers to avoid on-request cuda allocations.

Draft message to Helios SRE (internal copy):
Subject: Helios private deployment - tail latency spikes (investigating)
Hi Casey,
We’re actively investigating the latency spikes you observed 02/11–12. Initial evidence points to increased KV cache miss rates after the recent model rollout (v2.4.0) combined with transient GPU allocation failures in our runtime. We’ve taken short-term mitigations (increase kvcache, scaled up runtime replicas) which reduced error volume.
Request: can you hold traffic on canary cluster (if you have one) and avoid rolling further model updates until we validate a fix? Also please share any host-level NVMe/iostat logs for 22:00–23:30 UTC so we can rule out storage I/O as a contributor.
I’ll follow up with a summary once we have the root cause.
Thanks,
Maya (Redwood)

Notes to self / small TODOs:
- Ask model team for commit diff and tokenizer diff (Ravi assigned)
- Attach pprof+heap dumps to RED-4821 and link in Confluence
- Run a controlled canary: instrument runtime to pre-allocate kvcache buffers before first token generation
- Check PCIe errors: lspci -vvv and dmesg on node-3

Non-customer comms (Slack draft to #privdeploys):
Heads up: Helios saw tail latency spikes after v2.4.0 rollout; kvcache miss rate up, some CUDA OOMs. Rolling restart + kvcache increase helped; full rollback is on table if we can’t stabilize. Pinged model onboarding for key shape diff.

Random notes (extra logs/snips):
- runtime debug: "rehydrate_time p50=12ms p95=1.2s p99=4.9s"
- LB trace id: lb_hel_20250211_2212: 502 -> upstream read timeout after 6.0s
- local reproduction script: tests/loadgen/helios_kv_keyshape_test.py (branch: kv-keyshape-debug)

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a cleaner timeline and customer-facing postmortem if root cause confirmed.
summary: Scratchpad for Helios private-deploy incident: kvcache thrash after model rollout causing GPU allocation failures and tail latency spikes. Contains commands tried, errors, timeline, hypotheses, draft comms.
